subproblem.title: Graph integrals of a compactly supported covector field converge under C¹-flattening graphs and L¹_loc-convergent domains (parent Part D)
subproblem.statement: Let m, k, P ∈ ℕ, let ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be linear isometries (ℝ^d = Euclid d), b ∈ ℝ^k, R ∈ ℝ, B := ball(0, R) ⊆ ℝ^m, and let β : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) (Covector (Euclid P) m) be continuous with compact support. Let g_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^k (i ∈ ℕ) and let A_i, A ⊆ ℝ^m be measurable sets. Assume (a) L^m((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) → 0 (L^m = Lebesgue measure, Δ = symmetric difference); (b) for all large i, g_i is differentiable at every w ∈ B; (c) for every ε > 0, for all large i, |g_i(w) − b| < ε and ‖Dg_i(w)‖ < ε for all w ∈ B. Put G_i(w) := ιw + ι'g_i(w), DG_i(w) := fderiv ℝ G_i w and e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1. Then ∫_{A_i∩B} β(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e_0, …, DG_i(w)e_{m−1}) dw → ∫_{A∩B} β(ιw + ι'b)(ιe_0, …, ιe_{m−1}) dw as i → ∞ (Bochner integrals with respect to Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m k P : ℕ) (ι : Euclid m →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid P) (ι' : Euclid k →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid P) (b : Euclid k) (R : ℝ) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) m) (gs : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid k) (As : ℕ → Set (Euclid m)) (A : Set (Euclid m)), Continuous β → HasCompactSupport β → (∀ i, MeasurableSet (As i)) → MeasurableSet A → Tendsto (fun i => volume (symmDiff (As i) A ∩ ball (0 : Euclid m) R)) atTop (𝓝 0) → (∀ᶠ i in atTop, ∀ w ∈ ball (0 : Euclid m) R, DifferentiableAt ℝ (gs i) w) → (∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ i in atTop, ∀ w ∈ ball (0 : Euclid m) R, ‖gs i w - b‖ < ε ∧ ‖fderiv ℝ (gs i) w‖ < ε) → Tendsto (fun i => ∫ w in As i ∩ ball 0 R, β (ι w + ι' (gs i w)) (fun j => fderiv ℝ (fun w => ι w + ι' (gs i w)) w (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ w in A ∩ ball 0 R, β (ι w + ι' b) (fun j => ι (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ)))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Steps D1–D4 of the supplied proof of the parent node codim1_zsl_flat_graph_limit (uniform convergence of the integrands from the C¹ convergence g_i → b, and convergence of the integrals from the L¹_loc convergence of the indicators supplied by BV compactness; Simon 7.5.3, chapter-07.txt lines 848–852, "converges in L¹_loc", and 7.5.5, lines 862–901), stated for an arbitrary continuous compactly supported field of m-covectors β in place of dω and for arbitrary dimensions m, k, P. Departure: the uniform continuity argument of D2 is made explicit through the multilinear difference bound ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_image_sub_le and an ε-argument; no orthogonality of ι and ι' is needed.
Notation. h_i(w) := β(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e_0, …, DG_i(w)e_{m−1}) and h(w) := β(ιw + ι'b)(ιe_0, …, ιe_{m−1}); L := L^m; |·| Euclidean and operator norms; for u : Fin m → ℝ^P, ‖u‖ := max_j |u_j| (the sup norm, pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg).
1. Constants. β is continuous with compact support, hence bounded, |β(y)| ≤ M for all y with some M ≥ 0 (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), and uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). B is measurable with L(B) < ∞ (measure_ball_lt_top). |e_j| = 1 and |ιe_j| = 1.
2. The limit integrand. |h(w)| ≤ |β(ιw + ι'b)|·∏_j |ιe_j| ≤ M (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm), and h is continuous (w ↦ β(ιw + ι'b) is continuous and evaluation at the fixed family ιe is continuous, continuous_eval_const). Hence h is integrable on every set of finite measure (IntegrableOn.of_bound).
3. Derivative of G_i. If g_i is differentiable at w, then DG_i(w) = ι + ι'∘Dg_i(w) (derivative of the linear map ι plus chain rule for ι'∘g_i: HasFDerivAt.add, HasFDerivAt.comp), so DG_i(w)e_j = ιe_j + ι'(Dg_i(w)e_j).
4. Pointwise estimate. Let g_i be differentiable at w with ‖Dg_i(w)‖ ≤ 1; write T := Dg_i(w), y := G_i(w), y' := ιw + ι'b, u_j := DG_i(w)e_j, u'_j := ιe_j. Then |u_j| ≤ |ιe_j| + |ι'(Te_j)| ≤ 1 + ‖T‖ ≤ 2, |u'_j| = 1 and |u_j − u'_j| = |ι'(Te_j)| ≤ ‖T‖; so ‖u‖ ≤ 2, ‖u'‖ ≤ 1 and ‖u − u'‖ ≤ ‖T‖. Split h_i(w) − h(w) = [β(y)(u) − β(y')(u)] + [β(y')(u) − β(y')(u')]. The first bracket equals (β(y) − β(y'))(u) and is at most |β(y) − β(y')|·∏_j|u_j| ≤ 2^m·|β(y) − β(y')| in absolute value (le_opNorm). The second is at most |β(y')|·m·max(‖u‖, ‖u'‖)^{m−1}·‖u − u'‖ ≤ M·m·2^m·‖T‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_image_sub_le, 2^{m−1} ≤ 2^m). Hence |h_i(w) − h(w)| ≤ 2^m·|β(G_i(w)) − β(ιw + ι'b)| + M·m·2^m·‖Dg_i(w)‖.
5. Uniform convergence on B. Let ε > 0. By uniform continuity choose δ > 0 with |β(y) − β(y')| < ε/(2·2^m) whenever |y − y'| < δ. Put X := M·m·2^m ≥ 0 and η := min(1, ε/(2(X + 1))) > 0. By (b) and by (c) with δ and with η, for all large i and all w ∈ B: g_i is differentiable at w, |G_i(w) − (ιw + ι'b)| = |ι'(g_i(w) − b)| = |g_i(w) − b| < δ, and ‖Dg_i(w)‖ < η ≤ 1. By step 4, |h_i(w) − h(w)| ≤ 2^m·ε/(2·2^m) + X·ε/(2(X + 1)) ≤ ε/2 + ε/2 = ε. Thus for every ε > 0, for all large i, |h_i − h| ≤ ε on B.
6. Measurability. For every i such that g_i is differentiable on B, h_i is a.e.-strongly measurable with respect to L restricted to B: G_i is continuous at each point of B, hence continuous on B and a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞B (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable, B measurable); w ↦ DG_i(w) is measurable for an arbitrary map (measurable_fderiv), hence a.e.-strongly measurable (finite-dimensional target); and h_i(w) = Φ(G_i(w), DG_i(w)) with Φ(y, T) := β(y)(Te_0, …, Te_{m−1}), which is continuous on ℝ^P × L(ℝ^m, ℝ^P) (continuity of β and of T ↦ Te_j, and joint continuity of evaluation, continuous_eval). A continuous function of an a.e.-strongly measurable map is a.e.-strongly measurable. By (b) this holds for all large i.
7. Symmetric differences in ℝ. L((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) → 0 in [0, ∞] by (a), and toReal is continuous at 0 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), so the real numbers L((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) tend to 0.
8. Final estimate. Let ε > 0 and V := L(B) ∈ [0, ∞) (as a real number). By steps 5–7, for all large i simultaneously: |h_i − h| ≤ ε/(2(V + 1)) on B, |h_i − h| ≤ 1 on B, h_i is a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞B, and L((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) < ε/(4(M + 1)). Fix such i and put s := A_i ∩ B, t := A ∩ B (measurable, of finite measure). h_i is integrable on s (a.e.-strongly measurable for L⌞s since s ⊆ B, and |h_i| ≤ |h_i − h| + |h| ≤ 1 + M on s; IntegrableOn.of_bound), and h is integrable on s and on t (step 2). (a) |∫_s h_i − ∫_s h| = |∫_s (h_i − h)| ≤ ε/(2(V + 1))·L(s) ≤ ε/(2(V + 1))·V < ε/2 (integral_sub, norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const, L(s) ≤ L(B)). (b) ∫_s h = ∫_{s∩t} h + ∫_{s∖t} h and ∫_t h = ∫_{t∩s} h + ∫_{t∖s} h (integral_inter_add_sdiff), so ∫_s h − ∫_t h = ∫_{s∖t} h − ∫_{t∖s} h. A point of s ∖ t lies in B and in A_i but not in A, and a point of t ∖ s lies in B and in A but not in A_i; so both sets lie in (A_i Δ A) ∩ B, and |∫_s h − ∫_t h| ≤ M·L(s∖t) + M·L(t∖s) ≤ 2M·L((A_i Δ A) ∩ B) ≤ 2(M + 1)·ε/(4(M + 1)) = ε/2. Hence |∫_{A_i∩B} h_i − ∫_{A∩B} h| < ε for all large i. As ε > 0 was arbitrary, the integrals converge (Metric.tendsto_nhds). ∎

subproblem.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ, let ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be a linear isometry (ℝ^d = Euclid d), c ∈ ℝ^P, G(w) := ιw + c, and let A ⊆ ℝ^m be measurable. Then G(A) is a (Borel) measurable subset of ℝ^P, and for every function f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{G(A)} f dH^m = ∫_A f(G(w)) dw, where H^m = μHE[m] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure) on ℝ^P and dw is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^m; both sides are Bochner integrals (a non-integrable function has integral 0).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (ι : Euclid m →ₗᵢ[ℝ] Euclid P) (c : Euclid P) (A : Set (Euclid m)), MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet ((fun w => ι w + c) '' A) ∧ ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ y in (fun w => ι w + c) '' A, f y ∂μHE[m] = ∫ w in A, f (ι w + c)

Source. Steps E1–E2 of the supplied proof of the parent node codim1_zsl_flat_graph_limit (Hausdorff measure is invariant under isometries, and μHE[m] is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m), for an arbitrary linear isometry followed by a translation; Simon 7.5.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 862–901) regards the limit set F as an H^{n+1}-measurable subset of the plane T_xN in exactly this way.
1. G is an isometry: |G(x) − G(y)| = |ι(x − y)| = |x − y| (Isometry.of_dist_eq, add_sub_add_right_eq_sub, map_sub, LinearIsometry.norm_map). Since ℝ^m is complete, G is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), hence a measurable embedding (IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). In particular G is injective and G(A) is measurable (MeasurableEmbedding.measurableSet_image').
2. Push-forward. For an isometry, the push-forward of μHE[m] is μHE[m] restricted to the range (Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure), and on ℝ^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), μHE[m] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence G_#(volume on ℝ^m) = μHE[m]⌞range G.
3. Restriction. G(A) is measurable and G(A) ⊆ range G, so μHE[m]⌞G(A) = (μHE[m]⌞range G)⌞G(A) (Measure.restrict_restrict; G(A) ∩ range G = G(A)) = (G_#volume)⌞G(A) = G_#(volume⌞G⁻¹(G(A))) (MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map) = G_#(volume⌞A), because G⁻¹(G(A)) = A by injectivity (preimage_image_eq).
4. Integral. For every f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{G(A)} f dμHE[m] = ∫ f d(G_#(volume⌞A)) = ∫_A f(G(w)) dw (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, which holds for every integrand because G is a measurable embedding). ∎

subproblem.title: Divergence fields lift to normalised test forms near a flat graph: dω(G(v))(DG(v)e) = K⁻¹·div φ(v) with |ω| ≤ 1 (parent Part A)
subproblem.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, P := n + 1 + k, and let ι : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be linear isometries with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w and such that every y ∈ ℝ^P equals ιv + ι'w for some v, w (ℝ^d = Euclid d). Then there is a constant K > 0 with the following property. For all real h > 0 and R, and every C^∞ vector field φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ) with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ ball(0, R) and |φ(v)| ≤ 1 for all v, there is a test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) (ω : TestFormOn univ n, i.e. a C^∞ n-form on ℝ^P with compact support) such that: (i) tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R + 2h) ⊆ ℝ^P; (ii) covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for every y ∈ ℝ^P; (iii) for every map g : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^k and every v ∈ ℝ^{n+1} such that g is differentiable at v and |g(v)| < h, dω(ιv + ι'g(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n) = K⁻¹·div φ(v), where G(w) := ιw + ι'g(w), DG(v) := fderiv ℝ G v, e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1, dω := exteriorDerivative ω and div φ(v) := trace Dφ(v) (LinearMap.trace of (fderiv ℝ φ v)).

Source. Part A (steps A1–A6) of the supplied proof of the parent node codim1_zsl_flat_graph_limit (lifting divergence fields to test forms with a cut-off in the normal direction; uniform comass bound K), together with the normalisation ω/K of its step B3, which is built into the form here. Simon 7.5.3 (chapter-07.txt lines 790–860) uses this lifting implicitly when it applies the BV Compactness 2.6 of Ch. 2 to the rescaled regions. Departures from the supplied Part A, none of which changes the argument: (1) the contracted volume form Ω(z, ·) of A1–A2 is written Θ(z) = Σ_j z_j·β_j with the coordinate covectors β_j = e_j ⌟ det of the accepted sibling coordinate_covector (Submission.dgcr_bwd_coordinate_covector); this is the same covector because Ω(z, ·) = Σ_j z_j·Ω(e_j, ·); (2) the cut-off χ(|ι'*y|²) built from smoothTransition in A3 is replaced by f(ι'*y) for a ContDiffBump f on ℝ^k with radii h < 2h, which has the same properties (C^∞, values in [0, 1], = 1 where |ι'*y| ≤ h, = 0 where |ι'*y| ≥ 2h); (3) the constant K of A5 is explicit; (4) the identity d(π^#α̃)(G(v))(DG(v)e) = dα̃(v)(e) of A6 is the accepted sibling pullback_extderiv (Submission.dgcr_bwd_graph_pullback_extDeriv) with z = 0.
Notation. P := n + 1 + k; ℝ^d := Euclid d; e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ) ∈ ℝ^{n+1}, e := (e_0, …, e_n), and removeNth i e := Fin.removeNth i e (e with e_i deleted). π := ι* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap : ℝ^P → ℝ^{n+1} and π' := ι'* : ℝ^P → ℝ^k likewise. ‖·‖ denotes operator norms; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for an n-covector α on ℝ^P, b_l := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ l the standard basis of ℝ^P. (In Lean the smoothness order must be written (⊤ : ℕ∞): in the contract scope `∞` is ENNReal's ∞.)
1. Adjoint identities. For v ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and w ∈ ℝ^k: π(ιv) = v, π(ι'w) = 0, π'(ι'w) = w and π'(ιv) = 0. Indeed, for every y, ⟨π(ιv), y⟩ = ⟨ιv, ιy⟩ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_left) = ⟨v, y⟩ (LinearIsometry.inner_map_map), and ⟨π(ι'w), y⟩ = ⟨ι'w, ιy⟩ = ⟨ιy, ι'w⟩ = 0 by the orthogonality hypothesis (real_inner_comm); the same computation with the roles of ι and ι' exchanged gives the other two; vectors with the same inner product against every y are equal (ext_inner_right).
2. Norm splitting. For every y ∈ ℝ^P, |y| ≤ |πy| + |π'y|: write y = ιv + ι'w (spanning hypothesis); by step 1, πy = v and π'y = w, and |y| ≤ |ιv| + |ι'w| = |v| + |w|.
3. Coordinate covectors and Θ. By coordinate_covector with m := n, choose for every j ∈ Fin (n+1) an n-covector β_j on ℝ^{n+1} with β_j(removeNth i e) = (−1)^j if i = j and = 0 if i ≠ j. Let Θ : ℝ^{n+1} → Λ^n(ℝ^{n+1}) be the continuous linear map Θ := Σ_j (EuclideanSpace.proj j).smulRight β_j, i.e. Θ(z) = Σ_j z_j·β_j. Then for all z ∈ ℝ^{n+1} and i: Θ(z)(removeNth i e) = Σ_j z_j·β_j(removeNth i e) = (−1)^i·z_i (ContinuousAlternatingMap.sum_apply; only the summand j = i is nonzero).
4. The constant. Let N := card(Fin n → Fin P) (= P^n) and K := √N·‖Θ‖·‖π‖^n + 1 > 0. K depends only on n, k, ι (through the choice of the β_j and π), not on h, R or φ; this is the asserted constant. From now on fix h > 0, R and φ as in the statement.
5. The form. α̃ := Θ∘φ, i.e. α̃(v) = Σ_j φ_j(v)·β_j = Ω(φ(v), ·): a smooth n-form on ℝ^{n+1} (C^∞ map followed by a continuous linear map). Its affine pull-back P^#α̃ := affinePullbackForm π (−π0) α̃, (P^#α̃)(y) = α̃(−π0 + πy)∘π = α̃(πy)∘π, is a smooth n-form on ℝ^P (affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm). Let f be the ContDiffBump on ℝ^k centred at 0 with rIn = h and rOut = 2h (0 < h < 2h): f is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 (nonneg, le_one), f = 1 on closedBall(0, h) (one_of_mem_closedBall) and support f = ball(0, 2h) (support_eq). Define ω(y) := (K⁻¹·f(π'y))·(P^#α̃)(y). Then ω is C^∞, as the product of the C^∞ function y ↦ K⁻¹f(π'y) with the smooth form P^#α̃ (ContDiff.smul).
6. Support, (i) and ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P). Let Q := {y : πy ∈ tsupport φ and |π'y| ≤ 2h}; Q is closed (preimages of closed sets under continuous maps). If ω(y) ≠ 0 then f(π'y) ≠ 0, so π'y ∈ ball(0, 2h) and |π'y| ≤ 2h; and (P^#α̃)(y) ≠ 0, so φ(πy) ≠ 0 (otherwise α̃(πy) = Θ(0) = 0 and the pull-back vanishes), so πy ∈ tsupport φ. Hence the support of ω lies in Q, and tsupport ω ⊆ Q (closure_minimal). For y ∈ Q, πy ∈ tsupport φ ⊆ ball(0, R) gives |πy| < R, so by step 2 |y| ≤ |πy| + |π'y| < R + 2h. Thus tsupport ω ⊆ Q ⊆ ball(0, R + 2h), which is (i); and tsupport ω is a closed subset of the compact closedBall(0, R + 2h), so ω has compact support. Together with step 5, ω is a test form, and tsupport ω ⊆ univ trivially: ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
7. Comass bound (ii). Fix y ∈ ℝ^P and a strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P. By the definitions (affinePullbackForm, compContinuousLinearMap_apply), ω(y)(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)}) = K⁻¹f(π'y)·Θ(φ(πy))(πb_{I(0)}, …, πb_{I(n−1)}). Here |K⁻¹f(π'y)| ≤ K⁻¹, and by ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm |Θ(φ(πy))(πb_{I(·)})| ≤ ‖Θ(φ(πy))‖·∏_l |πb_{I(l)}| ≤ ‖Θ‖·|φ(πy)|·‖π‖^n ≤ ‖Θ‖·‖π‖^n (|b_l| = 1 and |φ| ≤ 1). So each of the at most N squared coefficients in |ω(y)|² is at most (K⁻¹‖Θ‖‖π‖^n)², whence |ω(y)|² ≤ N·(K⁻¹‖Θ‖‖π‖^n)² = (√N·K⁻¹‖Θ‖‖π‖^n)² ≤ 1 because √N‖Θ‖‖π‖^n ≤ K; taking square roots (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, Real.sqrt_one), covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1.
8. Key identity (iii): germ. Let g be differentiable at v with |g(v)| < h, and y₀ := ιv + ι'g(v). By step 1, π'y₀ = g(v), so y₀ lies in the open set {y : |π'y| < h}, on which f(π'y) = 1 (π'y ∈ closedBall(0, h)). Hence ω coincides with K⁻¹·P^#α̃ on a neighbourhood of y₀. The exterior derivative at a point depends only on the germ of the form there (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq; SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative is Mathlib's extDeriv) and d(c·β) = c·dβ (exteriorDerivative_smul). Therefore dω(y₀)(DG(v)e) = K⁻¹·d(P^#α̃)(y₀)(DG(v)e).
9. Key identity (iii): pull-back. Apply pullback_extderiv (Submission.dgcr_bwd_graph_pullback_extDeriv) with m := n, the given k, ι, ι', u := g, z := 0, ψ := α̃ (smooth by step 5) and the point v (g is differentiable at v; orthogonality hypothesis). It gives d(affinePullbackForm π (−π0) α̃)(0 + ιv + ι'g(v))(i ↦ D[w ↦ 0 + ιw + ι'g(w)](v)e_i) = dα̃(v)(e); deleting the summands 0 (zero_add), d(P^#α̃)(y₀)(DG(v)e) = dα̃(v)(e). With step 8: dω(y₀)(DG(v)e) = K⁻¹·dα̃(v)(e).
10. dα̃(v)(e) = div φ(v). The form α̃ is differentiable at v, so by the coordinate formula for d (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply), dα̃(v)(e) = Σ_i (−1)^i·D[x ↦ α̃(x)(removeNth i e)](v)e_i. By step 3, α̃(x)(removeNth i e) = Θ(φ(x))(removeNth i e) = (−1)^i·φ_i(x), where φ_i(x) := (φ(x))_i; by the chain rule with the coordinate projection EuclideanSpace.proj i, the derivative at v applied to e_i is (−1)^i·(Dφ(v)e_i)_i. Hence dα̃(v)(e) = Σ_i (−1)^i(−1)^i(Dφ(v)e_i)_i = Σ_i (Dφ(v)e_i)_i = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dφ(v)e_i⟩ = trace Dφ(v) (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner for the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun, and ⟨e_i, x⟩ = x_i by EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left). Combining with step 9: dω(ιv + ι'g(v))(DG(v)e_0, …, DG(v)e_n) = K⁻¹·div φ(v), which is (iii). ∎

  intro n k ι ι' hperp hspan
  classical
  set π : Euclid (n + 1 + k) →L[ℝ] Euclid (n + 1) :=
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ι.toContinuousLinearMap with hπeq
  set π' : Euclid (n + 1 + k) →L[ℝ] Euclid k :=

    intro z i

subproblem.title: Uniform local perimeter bounds for the parameter sets F_i from the mass bounds of the S_i (parent Part B)
subproblem.statement: Let n, k ∈ ℕ, P := n + 1 + k, U_i ⊆ ℝ^P and currents S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(U_i) (GeometricCurrentOn (U_i) n) for i ∈ ℕ, linear isometries ι : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^P and ι' : ℝ^k → ℝ^P with ⟨ιv, ι'w⟩ = 0 for all v, w and such that every y ∈ ℝ^P equals ιv + ι'w for some v, w, b ∈ ℝ^k, maps g_i : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^k and measurable sets F_i ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}; put G_i(w) := ιw + ι'g_i(w) and e_j := EuclideanSpace.single j 1. Assume, for every R > 0 (B_R := ball(0, R) ⊆ ℝ^{n+1}): (H1) for all large i, g_i is differentiable at every w ∈ B_R; (H2) for every ε > 0 and all large i, |g_i(w) − b| < ε and ‖Dg_i(w)‖ < ε for all w ∈ B_R; (H3) for all large i and every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R) ⊆ ℝ^P, currentEval(S_i)(ω) = ∫_{F_i∩B_R} dω(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e_0, …, DG_i(w)e_n) dw (DG_i(w) = fderiv ℝ G_i w); (H4) there is c ∈ ℝ such that for all large i and every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R) and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for all y, currentEval(S_i)(ω) ≤ c. Then for every R > 0 there is c ∈ ℝ such that, for all large i and every C^∞ vector field φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ) with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ B_R and |φ(v)| ≤ 1 for all v, ∫_{F_i} div φ dL^{n+1} ≤ c, where div φ(v) := trace Dφ(v) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ φ v) and L^{n+1} is Lebesgue measure. (This is the hypothesis of the sibling BV compactness theorem codim1_zsl_perimeter_compactness for the sets F_i, with m := n + 1.)

Departure: the normalisation ω/K of step B3 is already built into the test form of the sibling divergence_lift, so linearity of currentEval is not needed.
Notation: as in the statement; |·| are Euclidean norms, ‖·‖ operator norms, div φ := trace Dφ.
1. Constants. Let K > 0 be the constant of divergence_lift (Submission.codim1_zsl_fl_divergence_lift) for n, k, ι, ι' (its hypotheses are the orthogonality and spanning hypotheses). Fix R > 0 and put h := |b| + 1 > 0 and R₂ := R + 2h > 0. Let c₂ be the constant given by (H4) for R₂, and put c := K·c₂.
2. Large i. (H1) for R₂, (H2) for R₂ and ε := 1, (H3) for R₂ and the eventual statement of (H4) for R₂ each hold for all sufficiently large i, hence all four hold simultaneously for all large i (intersection of finitely many eventually-true statements). Fix such an i and a field φ as in the conclusion; it remains to show ∫_{F_i} div φ ≤ c.
3. The test form. divergence_lift applied to h, R and φ gives ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, R + 2h) = ball(0, R₂), covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(y)) ≤ 1 for all y, and dω(ιw + ι'g(w))(DG(w)e) = K⁻¹·div φ(w) whenever g is differentiable at w and |g(w)| < h. By (H4), currentEval(S_i)(ω) ≤ c₂; by (H3), currentEval(S_i)(ω) = ∫_{F_i∩B_{R₂}} dω(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e) dw.
4. The integrand on B_{R₂}. Let w ∈ B_{R₂}. By (H1), g_i is differentiable at w, and by (H2), |g_i(w)| ≤ |g_i(w) − b| + |b| < 1 + |b| = h. Step 3 with g := g_i gives dω(G_i(w))(DG_i(w)e) = K⁻¹·div φ(w). Since F_i ∩ B_{R₂} is measurable, the two integrands have the same integral over it (setIntegral_congr_fun), and ∫_{F_i∩B_{R₂}} K⁻¹·div φ = K⁻¹·∫_{F_i∩B_{R₂}} div φ (integral_const_mul).
5. Removing the ball. If w ∈ F_i \ B_{R₂} then w ∉ tsupport φ (because tsupport φ ⊆ B_R ⊆ B_{R₂}); since tsupport(Dφ) ⊆ tsupport φ (tsupport_fderiv_subset), Dφ(w) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and div φ(w) = trace 0 = 0. As F_i is measurable and F_i ∩ B_{R₂} ⊆ F_i, ∫_{F_i∩B_{R₂}} div φ = ∫_{F_i} div φ (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero).
6. Conclusion. Steps 3–5 give K⁻¹·∫_{F_i} div φ ≤ c₂; multiplying by K > 0 yields ∫_{F_i} div φ ≤ K·c₂ = c. ∎

  obtain ⟨K, hK, hlift⟩ := Submission.codim1_zsl_fl_divergence_lift n k ι ι' hperp hspan
  set h : ℝ := ‖b‖ + 1 with hh
  have hhpos : 0 < h := by positivity
  set R₂ : ℝ := R + 2 * h with hR₂
  have hR₂pos : 0 < R₂ := by positivity
  obtain ⟨c₂, hc₂⟩ := hH4 R₂ hR₂pos
  refine ⟨K * c₂, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hH1 R₂ hR₂pos, hH2 R₂ 1 hR₂pos one_pos, hH3 R₂ hR₂pos, hc₂] with i hi1 hi2 hi3 hi4
  intro φ hφ hφc hφs hφn
  obtain ⟨ω, hωs, hωn, hωd⟩ := hlift h R hhpos φ hφ hφc hφs hφn
  have hle := hi4 ω hωs hωn
  rw [hi3 ω hωs] at hle
  have hcongr : ∫ w in Fs i ∩ ball 0 R₂, exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid (n + 1 + k)) n)
        (ι w + ι' (gs i w)) (fun j => fderiv ℝ (fun w => ι w + ι' (gs i w)) w
          (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))) =
      ∫ w in Fs i ∩ ball 0 R₂, K⁻¹ * LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (n + 1)) (fderiv ℝ φ w).toLinearMap := by
    apply setIntegral_congr_fun ((hFs i).inter measurableSet_ball)
    intro w hw
    apply hωd (gs i) w (hi1 w hw.2)
    have := (hi2 w hw.2).1
    calc ‖gs i w‖ = ‖(gs i w - b) + b‖ := by rw [sub_add_cancel]
      _ ≤ ‖gs i w - b‖ + ‖b‖ := norm_add_le _ _
      _ < 1 + ‖b‖ := by linarith
      _ = h := by ring
  rw [hcongr, integral_const_mul] at hle
  have hdiv : ∫ w in Fs i ∩ ball 0 R₂, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (n + 1)) (fderiv ℝ φ w).toLinearMap =
      ∫ w in Fs i, LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid (n + 1)) (fderiv ℝ φ w).toLinearMap := by
    refine (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero (hFs i) inter_subset_left ?_).symm
    intro w hw
    have hwnot : w ∉ tsupport φ := fun hmem =>
      hw.2 ⟨hw.1, ball_subset_ball (by linarith) (hφs hmem)⟩
    have h0 : fderiv ℝ φ w = 0 :=
      image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport (fun hmem => hwnot (tsupport_fderiv_subset ℝ hmem))
    simp [h0]
  rw [hdiv] at hle
  have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hle hK.le
  rwa [← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel₀ hK.ne', one_mul] at this
proof_key_steps: Fix R > 0; h := |b| + 1, R₂ := R + 2h, c₂ from (H4) at R₂, c := K·c₂ with K from divergence_lift.
For all large i, (H1), (H2) with ε = 1, (H3) and (H4) hold at R₂ simultaneously.
divergence_lift gives an admissible ω supported in ball(0, R₂); (H4) gives currentEval(S_i)(ω) ≤ c₂ and (H3) represents it on F_i ∩ B_{R₂}.
On B_{R₂}, |g_i| < h and g_i is differentiable, so the integrand is K⁻¹·div φ; div φ vanishes off tsupport φ ⊆ B_R, so the integral is K⁻¹∫_{F_i} div φ.
Hence ∫_{F_i} div φ ≤ K·c₂ = c.

audit.reason: The eventual hypotheses are combined before quantifying over test fields. The normalized lift, H3 and H4 give the bound; vanishing divergence outside the support removes the ball, and positivity of K justifies rescaling. The conclusion exactly supplies the existing BV-compactness hypothesis without circularity.
